_meta.asset_kind: latinization declension paradigm -> genitive ending (one-dimensional model)
_meta.status: M0 draft. The genitive ending of a person-derived epithet is decided by the DECLENSION PARADIGM the surname was latinized into — not by the honoured person's sex and not by the stem's final letter. Only 'surnames' entries (each anchored to a published LPSN epithet) may be used to assert compliance; paradigm/defaults entries yield a proposal that is always flagged needs_review / compliant=None.
provenance: ICNP (2022) orthography rules on specific epithets formed from personal names: genitive of a latinized surname; the ending follows the paradigm chosen by the latinizer (-ius -> -ii, -a -> -ae, 3rd-declension -er -> -i).
LPSN (lpsn.dsmz.de) published epithets, cited per entry as 'lpsn_instances'.
The 2x2 'person gender x stem-final letter' table got 3 of 6 real names wrong (Burgdorfer -> burgdorferi, Hensel -> henselae, Gordon -> gordonae).
_meta.why_the_2x2_table_was_wrong: female_consonant_stem='iae' is correct only when the surname was latinized as a 1st-declension noun in -ia; the general 1st-declension ending is -ae, which applies to MALE honourees too (Hensel -> henselae, Gordon -> gordonae). Male consonant stems are not always -ii either (Burgdorfer -> burgdorferi). Gender therefore does not select the ending; the paradigm does, and the paradigm is only knowable from the published name.
_meta.counter_example_anchoring_the_v1_3_fix: Shigella boydii: feminine genus + male person -> boydii (a genitive noun does not decline with the genus gender).
_meta.how_to_extend: add the latinized surname (lowercase, latinized as by engine/orthography.latinize) with its paradigm, the published epithet and the source; set verified=true only with a published instance.

first_declension_a.latinization: surname cast as a 1st-declension noun in -a (nom. -a, gen. -ae)

second_declension_ius.latinization: surname cast as a 2nd-declension noun in -ius/-us (gen. -i), doubled -i- in the genitive by nomenclatural practice

third_declension_er.latinization: surname already ending in -er, treated as a 3rd-declension noun (Burgdorfer, gen. Burgdorferi)

first_declension_ia.latinization: surname cast as a 1st-declension noun in -ia (gen. -iae)
first_declension_ia.note: This is the ONLY situation in which the old female_consonant_stem='iae' cell held. No LPSN instance was inspected for this repository, so the paradigm is shipped unverified and any value taken from it is needs_review by construction.

third_declension_consonant.latinization: surname cast as a 3rd-declension consonant-stem noun (gen. -is)
third_declension_consonant.note: kept for completeness of the paradigm axis; never populated from memory, hence unverified.

defaults.note: usually right (Kitahara -> kitaharae) but the paradigm choice belongs to the latinizer
Burgdorfer -> burgdorferi; Bdellovibacter-style irregular stems exist, so never assert compliance
most common historical latinization for consonant-final surnames; a PROPOSAL only (Hensel/Gordon are the documented counter-examples -> -ae)

carries over the old female_consonant_stem='iae' cell, now explicitly marked unverified: it presupposes a -ia latinization. The general 1st-declension form would be -ae. Expert sign-off required either way.

variant_tolerance._note: Genuinely consumed by engine/validate.py::_person_genitive_result (the previous branch was dead because 'i' was not a value of any cell). Now that the 3rd-declension -er paradigm populates '-i', the pair {-i, -ii} is reachable.

genitive_i_ii.applies_when: the surname is NOT attested in 'surnames' with verified:true
genitive_i_ii.never_overrides: an attested published form (an attested mismatch is reported as non-compliant, with the tolerance named in the note)
genitive_i_ii.status: grading tolerance for benchmark B2; M0 list

variant_tolerance.double_consonants: tolerate single/doubled consonant spelling variants where LPSN records both (documentation only — not consumed by the engine)
